title: Soup at Camp
lines: The sun went down and camp got cold.
"Let us make soup for all of us," said Jen.
Jen, Sam and Max got out a big black pot.
Mom set the pot on the camp fire.
Then she sat at the table to watch them.
Sam threw in beans, corn and nuts.
Jen cut a peach and a pear into bits.
"It needs juice next," said Jen to Max.
Max went to the shed to get the juice.
He came back and threw it all in.
Then the soup went blue!
"Why is my soup blue?" said Jen.
Sam had a good look in the jug.
It was not juice. It was blue glue.
Max tried to spoon the glue back out.
But the blue had gone all the way down.
So the group had to start a new pot.
Mom gave them a clean pot and sat back down.
This time Jen looked at the jug first.
She let Max mix the juice in with a spoon.
The new soup was good and hot.
They ate it all up under the stars.

questions.ask: What made the soup turn blue?
questions.listenFor: Blue glue that Max threw in. Line fourteen says it.

questions.ask: What did Max think he was putting in?
questions.listenFor: Juice. Line nine says he went to get the juice.

questions.ask: How could the kids keep this from happening again? Why?
questions.listenFor: Any sensible answer - look at the jug first, keep glue out of the camp pot. Listen for the reason.
